annotator.notes: Student makes a common mistake of only subtracting one category from the total. Tutor guides them to account for all non-charcoal drawings first.

task_context.problem_statement: Thomas has 25 drawings to display. 14 of the drawings were made using colored pencils. 7 of the drawings were made using blending markers. The rest of the drawings were made with charcoal. How many are charcoal drawings?
task_context.reference_solution:
Thomas made 14 + 7 = <<14+7=21>>21 colored pencil and blending marker drawings.
Thomas made 25 total drawings – 21 colored pencil and blending marker drawings = <<25-21=4>>4 charcoal drawings.
#### 4

messages.content: I'm stuck on this problem: Thomas has 25 drawings to display. 14 of the drawings were made using colored pencils. 7 of the drawings were made using blending markers. The rest of the drawings were made with charcoal. How many are charcoal drawings? I think the answer is 11. Am I right?
I see you've come up with 11. To make sure we're on the right track, could you walk me through how you calculated that number?
Well, there are 25 drawings total and 14 are colored pencils, so I just did 25 minus 14 and got 11.

I see what you did there! You subtracted the colored pencil drawings from the total. However, take another look at the problem—are there any other types of drawings besides colored pencils and charcoal?
Oh, I forgot about the blending markers. There are 7 of those. Does that mean I subtract 7 from 11?

That is one way to approach it! Since you already removed the colored pencils, removing the blending markers from the remaining amount will leave you with just the charcoal drawings. What do you get when you do that?
11 minus 7 is 4. So the answer is 4 drawings?
That's correct! You successfully accounted for both the colored pencils and the blending markers to find the remaining charcoal drawings. Great job working through that.
